sections.html:
Green County splits the work between two offices near the courthouse. The Green County Sheriff collects the bill at 203 W Court Street, Greensburg, KY 42743, phone (270) 932-5641. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values every parcel from 103 South 1st Street in Greensburg, phone (270) 932-7518.

The PVA keeps the records and sets the assessment. The sheriff only takes payment. Go to the PVA for address changes, exemption forms and any question about how a value was reached. Call either office ahead to confirm hours, and ask for a payoff or a parcel record before you list the house.

The tax year starts with the January 1 assessment date and ends with the sheriff's settlement the following September. For a homeowner the dates that count are mid-September, when the sheriff receives the bills, November 1, when the discount ends, and January 1, when penalties begin. Delinquent certificates are normally offered for sale between July 14 and August 28.

Green County real estate tax calendar
StepDate or window
Public inspection of the roll, with PVA conferences13 days from the first Monday in May, Saturdays included
Assessment appeals board sits5 days, starting 25 to 35 days after inspection
Bills handed to the sheriffBy September 15
Discounted paymentBy November 1
Payment at face amountNovember 2 to December 31
Five percent penaltyJanuary 1 to 31
Ten percent penalty plus a 10 percent sheriff's add-onAfter January 31
Sheriff stops collecting; bills go to the clerkApril 15, at close of business
Sheriff's settlementBy September 1

If bills are mailed late, the state may move to a slower schedule that gives each step a 30-day stage.

The first stop is the Green County PVA and the second is the county clerk. Kentucky closes the local board to anyone who skipped the conference, and conferences take place during the May inspection window.

  • Let the PVA explain how the figure was reached, then state the value you think is right. The conference record shows the starting value, your claim and any changes you both accept.
  • File with the clerk before the workday ends on the day after the inspection period closes.
  • Come to the hearing with proof: lot and building details, insurance papers, build costs and listings of comparable houses.
  • When the board raises or lowers the value, it must give you a written reason.

Anyone you hire to speak for you must be on the state's list of qualified representatives and hold your written authorization. Skipping the filing or the hearing ends the path to the Kentucky Claims Commission. If the case finishes late and the board lands above your claim, expect a supplemental bill.

Section 170 of the Kentucky constitution exempts public property in public use, burial grounds, church property, charities, schools not run for gain, public libraries, household goods and crops in the producer's hands. A separate break serves owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and who keep the house as a permanent residence.

That break is worth $49,100 off assessed value in assessment years 2025 and 2026. Apply at the PVA with a birth certificate, license or passport. Disability claims need payments received through the whole assessment period and a yearly renewal, except for service-connected disabilities and owners with a permanent total disability finding.

If you move out, give the PVA your new mailing address so assessment notices and tax bills reach you.

A tax debt travels with the land and lands on the buyer unless it is cleared first. The owner on January 1 is personally liable, and the lien on a delinquent bill can survive 11 years under KRS 134.015 and 134.420, whoever holds title.

Timing drives the cost. If you pay the sheriff before April 15, you owe only the penalties already earned. After the transfer, the clerk adds 1 percent monthly interest, a 10 percent commission, a county attorney commission and a lien fee. The state's own worked example shows a bill growing quickly once the attorney's first notice goes out.

The county attorney writes at the 30-day and 60-day marks, and a sale follows 90 to 135 days after the transfer. Before listing, get both payoffs in writing, one from the sheriff for the current year and one from the clerk for anything transferred. The closing agent can then pay them from the sale proceeds. A cash sale that closes in a couple of weeks can head off the clerk's added charges if your bill is still with the sheriff.

sections.h2: Reading the penalty schedule as a seller
sections.html:
The calendar tells you what a delay costs. Closing before November 1 means the bill can still be paid with the discount, so a seller who has the bill in hand can pay early and hand the buyer a clean record. From November 2 through December 31 the face amount is due and nothing extra is added. January adds 5 percent. After January 31 the penalty rises to 10 percent, and the sheriff's own 10 percent add-on comes with it.

After April 15 the sheriff no longer collects. The bill moves to the clerk, and from then on interest, commissions and fees pile up month by month. If your closing date falls near one of these steps, ask the sheriff or clerk which figure applies on that exact day.

Green County is in south central Kentucky. Its only incorporated city is the seat, Greensburg, and Summersville is a census-designated place. The land covers about 286 square miles, and the Green River crosses it from east to west. Population was 11,644 in July 2025, up 4.8 percent from 2020, with 4,421 households. About 77.6 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. Median home value is $125,000, and median owner costs run $955 a month with a mortgage and $361 without. Median gross rent is $610.

The county sits on the Central and Eastern time zone line, with LaRue and Taylor counties to the north on Eastern time, so check which clock an appointment uses.

sections.h2: What to have ready before you list
sections.html:
Gather your last tax bill, the parcel number if you know it, and any exemption paperwork. Ask the sheriff whether the current year is paid, and ask the clerk whether older years were transferred after April 15. Have the PVA confirm your mailing address so notices follow you after the sale.

Buyers and title companies look at the same records, so surprises are rare when you check first. A house with a recorded lien can still sell, but the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, and a written figure from the clerk prevents a last-minute scramble.

faqs.q: When does the Green County discount end?
faqs.a: On November 1. The calendar lets owners pay 2 percent less through that date, face amount from the next day to December 31, and adds 5 percent in January.

faqs.q: Who takes tax payments in Green County?
faqs.a: The Green County Sheriff, at 203 W Court Street in Greensburg, phone (270) 932-5641. The PVA at (270) 932-7518 values property and handles exemptions but takes no payments.

faqs.q: What happens to a Green County bill after January 31?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty and a 10 percent sheriff fee apply. The clerk takes over on April 15 and charges monthly interest.

faqs.q: How large is the Green County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, get $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Apply at the PVA with proof of age or disability.

faqs.q: When does Green County sell delinquent tax bills?
faqs.a: The standard calendar lists July 14 through August 28, which falls 90 to 135 days after the April 15 handoff to the clerk.
